Was 15 x 23.5 ft running north-south; is now 20.51 x 18.68 running EAST-WEST, with a new entry vestibule off the south wall and the anchor moved (-7.9, +8.1) ft. Every wall assignment in this file was re-derived from scratch (see _wall_derivation). The headline change: THE DRESSER IS NO LONGER ON THE HEADBOARD WALL. Round 2 and 3 spent themselves solving a four-way collision on one 15 ft wall; the re-trace gives the dresser its own 13.26 ft west wall and the collision simply stops existing. Also this round: real cut openings replace the flush-decal windows, a vaulted ceiling re-derived for the rotated room, contact shadows under every piece, four readable pillows, and every tone value re-metered after the daylight.js change. Build scripts: tools/roomkit/build/room14/r4_*.py; run r4_place.py to rebuild + re-place + re-cut everything idempotently.

THE PANE IS DELIBERATE: the judged view is single-floor presentation mode, where floorview.js swaps the sky for a dark studio backdrop, so a bare hole reads as a BLACK rectangle — the opposite of the photo's blown-out windows. The hole carries the dollhouse read from outside; the pane carries the interior read.
_tone_note: EVERY VALUE IN THIS FILE WAS RE-METERED IN ROUND 4 and the round-2/3 numbers were all too bright — daylight.js raised the hemisphere ground and the daytime IBL after round 3. Three things were learned re-doing it, and they are worth more than the numbers: (a) tone.py's analytic exposure-1.15 -> ACES inverse NO LONGER PREDICTS THE RENDER. It is still right for reading the photo, but solving a material through it overshoots; the round-4 materials are solved on two-point log-linear fits measured off real renders instead (see r4_base.FIT and r4_ceiling's _L0/_B0/_L1/_B1). (b) An object's material collects ~1.7x the light a ROOM WALL of the same albedo and orientation does — models.js sets envMapIntensity on model materials. A gable infill solved on the wall's own number came out 238 against a 225 wall and left a visible seam across the whole room. (c) A DOWNWARD-facing plane still collects almost nothing (0.095), which is why the ceiling is the one surface that legitimately needs emissive. NO room-filling emissive box was added — critics flagged those as hard-edged panels.

Ceiling.note: ROUND 5 rebuilt from r4_ceiling as r5_ceiling.py for ONE bug fix and nothing else: the six recessed cans rendered as white blobs on the FLOOR from the dollhouse poses. roomkit.glb.cylinder() winds both end caps the same way, so its bottom cap faces UP; with double_sided=False (which the ceiling needs so its slopes cull from above) that left one bright emissive disc per can facing up through the culled ceiling, and at a 50 deg dollhouse elevation a disc 14 ft up projects onto the floor. Each can is now a single explicitly-wound DOWN-facing disc. REBUILT for the rotated room (r4_ceiling.py). RIDGE RUNS NORTH-SOUTH at local x 10.50, peak 14.60, eaves 8.00; west slope 32.2 deg (7.54:12), east 33.4 deg (7.91:12). h(x) = 8 + 6.6*x/10.50 west of the ridge and 8 + 6.6*(20.51-x)/10.01 east. HOW THE RIDGE WAS RE-DERIVED: round 3's two measured facts both survive — the gable's apex sits OVER THE BED (photo x ~712) and the apex stands ~358 px above the eave line at ~53 px/ft on the north wall, i.e. 6.6-6.75 ft of rise over an 8 ft wall. What does NOT survive is round 3's 35.8/47.3 deg split: that asymmetry was forced by squeezing an apex-over-the-bed into a 15 ft wall and is an artifact of the wrong footprint. On the real 20.51 ft wall the NW corner projects to photo x ~427 and the NE corner to ~980, so the apex at 712 sits at 51.5% of the wall = local x 10.56; the plan's bed centre is 10.40 and the room centre 10.255, and all three agree inside 0.3 ft. The pitch RELATIONSHIP is kept — the ridge is still east of the room centre so the west plane is still the shallower one — it is just no longer extreme. 32-33 deg is a 7.6:12 roof, which is how a house like this is framed. COVERAGE follows the real L: slopes run z 0..18.68 over the vestibule's x band (7.86..15.58) and z 0..13.26 elsewhere, plus six vertical infills — the full north gable, two main-south trapezoids either side of the vestibule, the vestibule's own south gable which crosses the ridge, and the vestibule's two side walls. WINDING IS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: _fan() takes the normal of the first triangle and flips the whole fan if it points the wrong way (round 3 once shipped the north gable backwards and you saw sky through it). TONE: slope bands carry emissive (a downward plane collects only 0.095 here) at photo ratios 1.075..0.962 west and 0.962..1.010 east of a 225 wall; the vertical gable infills carry pure ALBEDO and no emissive at all, solved on the measured object-material curve — see _tone_note (b). Six recessed cans lie in the slope planes, rotated by the slope angle.

Master Floor Shadows.note: NEW in round 4 — the round-1/round-3 critics' most-repeated finding was that nothing in this house has a contact shadow except what the Rug bakes, so everything floats. Soft dark decals on the slab under Dresser, Tall Chest, Nightstand, Desk, Foreground Chest, Chair and the head of the Bed (the part that overhangs the rug). Built as SIX NESTED translucent black frames (core alpha 0.42 falling to 0.03 at 0.72 ft of pad) rather than stacked quads, so nothing is coplanar and there is no z-fighting; at four rings the falloff still read as a grey mat with a visible step. Named with 'floor' in it ON PURPOSE: objects.js's SURFACE_RE makes it unpickable, which a room-wide decal must be or it swallows every click in the room. TWO TRAPS, both hit: (a) pos.y 0.005 renders NOTHING — house.js draws the room slab at y 0.01 and objects.js writes pos.y into the same space, so the decal was under the floor; (b) 0.018 still loses, because the slab carries polygonOffsetFactor -1 which pulls it toward the camera in depth by more than a few thousandths of a foot. 0.05 ft (0.6 in) wins and is not visible as a lift from any pose this room is judged from. Footprints are hard-coded in r4_shadows.FEET — re-run it if anything moves.

_round5: ROUND 5 - the bed, the textures and the density. (1) THE BED IS A KING. Round 3 'proved' a queen off the photo and rounds 3-4 carried it, while THIS FILE contradicted itself: _wall_derivation records the plan's bed icon at x 6.85..13.95 (7.10 ft) and _north_wall_budget then built a 5.35 ft queen inside it. The queen reading was a camera artifact - the photo is shot from the room's EAST side, so the headboard is ~25 deg off square and foreshortens by a quarter. Re-measured against things at the SAME depth: the two shams span 235 px where the headboard cap spans 283 px for 7.10 ft (39.9 px/ft), so each sham is 2.95 ft - a 36 in KING pillow. (2) EVERY SOFT SURFACE IS NOW A TONE FIELD (build/room14/r5_raster.py), not a height field. Round 4 metered rug sigma 3.6 / duvet 2.8 against the photo's ~18 local / ~12; this scene has one sun and a large isotropic hemisphere term, so a 20 deg normal tilt buys nothing - contrast has to be ALBEDO. Round 5 meters rug 15.3, duvet 6.3..8.5 local / 17.1 broad, shams 5.7..6.5 local / 14.0 broad. (3) The invented white Tall Chest is DELETED and the photo's pale ARMCHAIR + LEANING MATTRESS PANELS stand there instead. (4) Density: bags + folded laundry on the dresser, a plant, a second lamp, a bin, tablet/bottle/speaker on the nightstand, a sill cushion, two floor vents, a laundry hamper. (5) The wall TV from Master Bed 2 is built. (6) The dresser is rebuilt with FOUR drawers (two over one over one) and real plank grain. (8) BUG FIXED: the recessed cans rendered as white blobs on the FLOOR from the dollhouse poses - roomkit.glb.cylinder winds BOTH end caps the same way, so with double_sided=False the up-facing cap survived the ceiling's back-face cull. They are single down-facing discs now. PAYLOAD: the room went 3.41 MB -> 1.74 MB (rug 1.13 -> 0.14, wall art 1.43 -> 0.32). Build scripts: build/room14/r5_*.py; run r5_place.py.
